findings.body: The compatibility user storage accepts the same bearer recovery code indefinitely, defeating the one-time-use protection provided by the local recovery-code provider.
findings.failure_mode: Authentication succeeds repeatedly with one recovery code instead of advancing through and exhausting the recovery-code set.
findings.impact: The compatibility user storage accepts the same bearer recovery code indefinitely, defeating the one-time-use protection provided by the local recovery-code provider.
findings.root_cause: The new federated validator only checks membership in the stored code list and never updates that list after successful validation.
findings.suggested_fix: On a successful match, atomically remove the matched code from the stored list and persist the updated credential; add coverage that rejects reuse of a consumed code.
findings.title: Federated recovery codes are never consumed after successful validation
findings.trigger: A user authenticates through the newly added federated recovery-code path and then submits the same recovery code again.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 340 exists verbatim in the patch. The new federated validator at BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() checks if the input code exists in generatedKeys via anyMatch but never removes the matched code from the stored list. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode() after successful validation, but this federated path does not. This allows the same recovery code to be reused indefinitely, defeating one-time-use protection.

raw_findings.body: The subsequent removeStoredCredentialById call operates on local/federated Keycloak storage rather than the external user-storage provider, so the exhausted credential remains configured; the next recovery-code form rendering can fail because there is no next code.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Successful final-code authentication leaves stale external credential state and can cause a failure when the recovery-code input page requests a nonexistent next code.
raw_findings.impact: The subsequent removeStoredCredentialById call operates on local/federated Keycloak storage rather than the external user-storage provider, so the exhausted credential remains configured; the next recovery-code form rendering can fail because there is no next code.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch broadens credential lookup to federated credentials without adding a federated counterpart to the existing local-storage removal path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle exhaustion through an explicit user-storage delete/clear operation, or ensure the federated provider stops returning and reporting the exhausted credential before the next authentication attempt.
raw_findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credentials are removed from the wrong storage
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user-storage validator consumes the final recovery code, after which the authenticator receives an exhausted federated credential and enters the success branch.

raw_findings.body: createFromValues creates a new model without copying myUser.recoveryCodes' ID, so the returned recovery credential has a null identifier and cannot be reliably addressed for deletion or updates.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Credential-management responses expose an unusable null credential ID, breaking operations that target the federated recovery credential.
raw_findings.impact: createFromValues creates a new model without copying myUser.recoveryCodes' ID, so the returned recovery credential has a null identifier and cannot be reliably addressed for deletion or updates.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new user-storage getCredentials implementation rebuilds the model from raw values instead of preserving the existing CredentialModel identity.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the stored credential identifier when reconstructing the model, for example by setting the reconstructed model's ID from myUser.recoveryCodes.getId(), and retain the other stored metadata as well.
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery credential reconstruction drops its identifier
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user with configured recovery codes lists credentials through account or other credential-management APIs.

raw_findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean obtains numbers starting at 1, but the test asserts that the requested number is 0 and therefore fails before completing the login flow.

raw_findings.impact: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean obtains numbers starting at 1, but the test asserts that the requested number is 0 and therefore fails before completing the login flow.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test treats the displayed recovery-code number as zero-based even though createFromValues assigns numbers with i + 1.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Align the test with the one-based RecoveryAuthnCodeRepresentation numbering and convert the displayed code number to a zero-based list index when selecting recoveryKeys.
raw_findings.title: The recovery-code integration test uses the wrong code index
raw_findings.trigger: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin reaches the recovery-code page, where the model reports the first code's number.

raw_findings.body: The regression suite can pass without detecting that bearer recovery codes remain reusable.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A security-critical regression in federated recovery-code lifecycle handling is not detected by the integration test.
raw_findings.impact: The regression suite can pass without detecting that bearer recovery codes remain reusable.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added test covers only initial setup and one successful authentication, omitting the consumption and reuse behavior that distinguishes recovery codes from reusable passwords.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After the initial login, start another login using the same code and assert rejection, then verify that the next code succeeds and that exhaustion triggers recovery-code reconfiguration.

This means the returned credential model has null ID, breaking operations that need to address the credential by ID.
